A closed stateless cursor binds result, request, profile, ordering, and next position.
A cursor without its request binding is incomplete.
Rule-specific scope is explicitly discriminated.
A path selector without the required repository root cannot select scope precedence.
The exact result definition accepts the complete result vector.
A snapshot rejects a non-array entry ledger.
A report rejects a non-array result ledger.
A qualification sidecar requires an approval-evidence array.
A diagnostic header requires a structured terminal coverage ledger.
A diagnostic requires a structured decision trace.
A problem rejects a non-identifier code.
A revision requires an identity-bearing tree.
A profile requires a semantics-artifact array.
An analyzer requires immutable implementation artifacts.
A promotion record requires its threshold ledger.
An analysis key requires the exact structured budgets.
An exception requires its revision freshness pin.
An effective policy requires structured provenance closure.
A non-decided header forbids a verdict.
An understood extension may affect core semantics.
A preserved extension cannot affect core semantics.
A target extension disposition binds its exact target identifier.
A target disposition cannot omit its target identity.
A request disposition cannot invent a target identity.
A decided resolution carries a verdict.
A non-decided resolution forbids a verdict.
Envelope registries require ranked envelope-version entries.
Envelope registry entries require a safe integer ordering rank.
Windows backslash spelling cannot alias a portable POSIX path.
A schema-valid snapshot is rejected after validation when two entries have the same Unicode 17 case-fold key.
A schema-valid overlay cannot contain case-fold aliases in its operation path collection.
Distinct binding selector spellings cannot alias under the pinned Unicode 17 casefold/NFC collision key.
The generated registry-value fragment document has a closed empty root.
The generated registry-value fragment document rejects invented root fields.
The envelope-version discriminator owns numeric ID and replacement typing, so a non-self future replacement is structurally possible.
Discriminator-owned envelope typing does not weaken ordinary registry IDs or replacements to numeric versions.
Problem codes are closed to the problems registry and reject an identifier-shaped typo.
Diagnostic next actions are closed to the actions registry.
Remediation action IDs are closed to the actions registry.
Conformance claims bind a registered canonicalization profile ID.
The canonicalization profile version must equal the registered ID's @version suffix.
Canonicalization claims cannot substitute a registered profile from another role.
Diagnostic header wire codes are closed to the diagnostics registry.
Detailed diagnostic wire codes are closed to the same diagnostics registry.
The mixed-batch evidence binds two exact target inputs.
A decided and indeterminate target coexist with per-target coverage and one exact aggregate.
Snapshot paths require the exact versioned portable-path profile role.
Overlay identities reject a canonicalization profile substituted for the path profile.
Effective-policy path surfaces are bound to the portable-path profile role.
Binding path selectors carry the exact versioned portable-path profile reference.
The standalone request wire supplies exact pre-decode bytes for accounting.
A governed standalone exception rejects a non-NFC scope.
A governed standalone exception rejects a segment over 255 UTF-8 bytes.
A governed exception rejects profile-role substitution.
An effective policy and its exception must bind the same path profile.
Distinct policy path spellings cannot alias under the pinned collision key.
The exact same accepted path spelling may be referenced by different rules.
Distinct binding scope spellings cannot alias under the pinned collision key.
Bindings reject a profile from outside the accounting role.
Analysis keys reject a profile from outside the accounting role.
